items.recapEn: A dry autumn wind blew through Kakegawa castle town. Every time they rested Ken cooked; while Hana slept he bought Kakegawa tea; Yokoyama-san, a park volunteer, lent him the park kitchen for tea rice. Tanaka-san had predicted calm all day. At sunset the wind dropped as nobody predicted, and Ken said, "While it is quiet, eat."

items.recapEn: Sitting out of the wind in the castle park, Hana teased Ken for cooking every time they stop; he shot back that she writes every time they stop. Today's menu, he said, depends on the weather. Yokoyama-san offered the park kitchen, Hana's hat flew off, and they agreed to eat once the wind settled.

items.recapEn: A notice in Kakegawa Castle Park: the grounds are open all day, but building hours change by season and the buildings may close in strong wind. Shoes off inside, no eating or drinking in the buildings, the park kitchen by application at reception, groups a week ahead, trash taken home, inquiries at the park office.
